subject: Animation
title: Wes Anderson's Stop-Motion Vision
description: One-minute skill: Wes Anderson's Stop-Motion Vision.

hook.text: Wes Anderson directed two stop-motion films — Fantastic Mr. Fox and Isle of Dogs — with obsessive detail.

buildup.text: Anderson insisted on real fur, fabric, and materials. Every prop was handcrafted to his exact specification.

discovery.text: Fantastic Mr. Fox deliberately showcased the jerky motion of stop-motion rather than hiding it.

twist.text: Anderson directed remotely via email, sending animators incredibly detailed notes from across the world.

climax.text: Both films proved that A-list directors could bring artistic prestige to stop-motion filmmaking.

punchline.text: A perfectionist director found his perfect medium in puppets.

quiz.question: How did Wes Anderson approach stop-motion differently from other directors?
options: He used CGI to smooth all puppet movements
He embraced the jerky motion and insisted on handcrafted real materials for every prop
He only directed voice actors, not animators
